name: Synthesis Collective Cleanroom Isolation Suit
description:
A positive-pressure cleanroom suit that maintains a filtered, sterile micro-environment around the wearer. The suit's air supply is HEPA-filtered and pressurized slightly above ambient, ensuring that any breach pushes clean air out rather than allowing contaminants in. Transparent face panels provide full visibility.

Used in substrate research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and any environment where the work requires contamination levels measured in parts per billion. The suit protects the work from the wearer as much as it protects the wearer from the work.
functionality: Positive-pressure isolation, HEPA-filtered air, sterile micro-environment
what_it_says: You are the contaminant, and this suit keeps your biology from ruining something worth more than you.
story_hooks: A cleanroom suit's pressure logs show it was deliberately depressurized for eleven seconds during a substrate handling operation — just long enough to introduce the wearer's biological material into the sample.

physical_description.visual_profile: A full-body hermetic envelope that reads as medical-industrial rather than fashion—sleek, almost alien in its completeness. The suit creates a smooth, featureless silhouette broken only by the large transparent polycarbonate face panel and articulated joint reinforcements. Worn, it transforms the wearer into a walking laboratory: anonymous, clinical, other.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tailored through the torso and limbs for mobility without gaps; the suit is engineered rather than cut for comfort. Wrists and ankles seal with magnetic friction-locks. Slight positive pressure creates subtle inflation under the synthetic skin.
physical_description.primary_material: Multi-layer ballistic weave with integrated HEPA membrane—outer layer is treatment-resistant synth-polymer, middle layers are filtration media, inner layer is breathable moisture-wicking composite. All seams are heat-welded.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost frictionless outer surface with a subtle sheen; slight pneumatic give when touched. The face panel is optically clear polycarbonate with anti-fog nano-coating. Sleeves have reinforced textured grip panels at fingertips for precision work.
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical white with high-contrast charcoal gray at pressure seals, joint reinforcements, and the angular neck collar. Accent piping in medical-grade blue runs along seams. The face panel frame is matte gunmetal.
physical_description.closures: Full posterior magnetic seal-line from neck to tailbone, with redundant locking tabs. Wrist and ankle ports use screw-threaded magnetic couplers for glove and boot attachment. No visible zippers—all closures are pressure-sealed.
distinctive_features: Transparent polycarbonate face panel with 180-degree visibility
Integrated air intake valve on left shoulder (pressure gauge visible beneath)
Articulated joint reinforcements at elbows, knees, and spine
Synthesis Collective logo—a precise geometric circle—laser-etched on chest
Luminescent pressure-status indicator strip along spine (changes color if seal compromised)
Magnetic coupling ports for external tools and sensors
Fine texture grid on torso for static dissipation
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corpo equipment—prohibitively expensive, single-user, purpose-built. Ownership signals access to controlled research environments and substrate-level work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by pharmaceutical technicians, substrate researchers, and specialized medical personnel. Wearing one casually outside a cleanroom is a status marker—it says you work on problems that matter enough to require contamination control. Also worn ironically by some Tier 3 street techs who've salvaged used suits.
physical_description.condition_typical: When properly maintained: pristine, with crystalline clarity in the face panel. Used units show minor scratches on the panel and slight discoloration in the neck seal from repeated sweat exposure. Salvaged Tier 5 versions are often yellowed, scuffed, with questionable seal integrity.

image_prompt: Neo-noir fashion photography: a figure in a Synthesis Collective cleanroom isolation suit standing in a sterile laboratory environment, posed as if mid-work at a substrate station. The suit is clinical white with charcoal-gray seals and medical-blue piping, the transparent face panel reflecting soft blue laboratory lighting. The wearer's face is visible but anonymized behind the clear polycarbonate—expression irrelevant. Moody, cold lighting casts sharp shadows across the suit's pneumatic form. Dark chrome workbench and nebulous urban skyline visible through floor-to-ceiling windows in the background. Composition emphasizes the suit's geometric perfection and the wearer's transformation into a sterile instrument. High contrast, desaturated palette with neon blue accents.
